Caveman is perfect for the intermediate messages an agent emits while working (status notes, quick acks between tool calls): that is where the token volume is. **What happen**

```
On Windows with Git Bash as the shell, the `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` as a MSYS/Git Bash Unix-style path (e.g. `/c/Users/username/.claude/...`), but node.exe is a native Windows binary that cannot resolve this format. Node interprets the leading `/c/` as a relative path on the current drive, producing a garbled path like `D:\c\Users\username\.claude\...`.

Debug log:
```

node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1210
  throw err;

## Feature request: Support Bun as an installation runtime

### Problem

The Windows installer currently requires **Node.js ≥18**:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

I use **Bun** as my JavaScript runtime and package manager, and I do not have Node.js/npm installed. Bun can run most Node-compatible JavaScript/TypeScript tooling and provides equivalents for common workflows such as `npx` via `bunx`.

Because the installer explicitly checks for Node, users who use Bun-only environments cannot install Caveman even when Bun could
items.title: Add Bun support as an alternative installer runtime

items.author: AmirF194
items.body:
## Idea

The biggest remaining token waste isn't wording — it's assistants reprinting a 300-line file to change one line. Caveman's SKILL.md already bans decorative fluff and raw log dumps; the same principle extends naturally to code output:

**Proposed addition to `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` Rules section** (exact wording for your edit/veto):

> Code changes: show smallest diff, not whole file. Patch block, changed function, or `- old` / `+ new` lines with 1-2 context lines. Full file only when user ask, file is new, or most of file change anyway.
>
> Follow-up answers: only the delta. No rest
items.title: proposal: diff-first output rule — never reprint a full file for a local change
